title: Static analysis as tests
subtitle: Static checks run as tests in my governance platform: a carve gate on imports, a check that no hook can surface a non-operation.

stats.label: tokens of tool schemas replaced by one description
tools across three servers behind that description
characters, the cap a test holds the description to

lede: AgentOS once had a test that built a real store and wrote synthetic rows into the real work graph. I had a test added to the hook crate that scans the crate's own source and fails the build if any test constructs a store outside the isolated path. Test isolation became a property of the build, enforced by a source scan that sees a structural rule no unit test can. Agent Swarm needed its runtime to stay separable from the estate it grew up in, so a carve gate in CI fails the build when a product crate imports platform-specific code.
quote: When a rule breaks once, I add a test that fails the build for the whole class of mistake.
evidence: Static analysis as tests: source-scanning tests and a CI carve gate that fail the build for a whole class of mistake, such as any test building a store outside the isolated path.
FFI safety across Rust and CUDA: layout tests that compare the Rust and C views of every shared struct and fail the build when they diverge.
Design budgets enforced in CI: a test caps the one tool description that replaced 41,990 tokens of schemas for 44 tools at 520 characters.
author: Corey James
